rename.from: Rails 5.1.0.beta1 crashes on Heroku (cedar-14 or heroku-16). From v5.0.1. Error R10 (Boot timeout) -> Web process failed to bind to $PORT within 60 seconds of launch
rename.to: Rails 5.1.0.beta1 crashes on Heroku (cedar-14 or heroku-16). (v5.0.1 instead works fine). Error R10 (Boot timeout) -> Web process failed to bind to $PORT within 60 seconds of launch

body:
Looking at the logs I see this:

```
Feb 26 06:05:22 myApp app/web.1:  * Listening on tcp://localhost:58126 
```

That doesn't seem right to me - what values do you get in Rails 5.0.1. Also what's in your Procfile?
I don't have a Procfile. With 5.0.1 I did not need. I need one? How to?

Changing in Gemfile the Rails version to 5.0.1 this is the log:

```
Feb 26 09:17:07 myApp heroku/web.1:  State changed from crashed to starting 
Feb 26 09:17:09 myApp heroku/web.1:  Starting process with command `bin/rails server -p 54743 -e production` 
Feb 26 09:17:12 myApp app/web.1:  /app/vendor/bundle/ruby/2.4.0/gems/activesupport-5.0.1/lib/active_support/xml_mini.rb:51: warning: constant ::Fixnum is deprecated 
Feb 26 09:17:13 myApp app/web.1:  /app/vendor/bundle/ruby/2.4.0/gems/activesupport-5.0.1/lib/active_support/xml_mini.rb:52: warning: constant ::Bignum is deprecated 
Feb 26 09:17:13 myApp app/web.1:  /app/vendor/bundle/ruby/2.4.0/gems/activesupport-5.0.1/lib/active_support/core_ext/numeric/conversions.rb:138: warning: constant ::Fixnum is deprecated 
Feb 26 09:17:14 myApp app/web.1:  /app/vendor/bundle/ruby/2.4.0/gems/activejob-5.0.1/lib/active_job/arguments.rb:38: warning: constant ::Fixnum is deprecated 
Feb 26 09:17:14 myApp app/web.1:  /app/vendor/bundle/ruby/2.4.0/gems/activejob-5.0.1/lib/active_job/arguments.rb:38: warning: constant ::Bignum is deprecated 
Feb 26 09:17:15 myApp app/web.1:  => Booting Puma 
Feb 26 09:17:15 myApp app/web.1:  => Rails 5.0.1 application starting in production on http://0.0.0.0:54743 
Feb 26 09:17:15 myApp app/web.1:  => Run `rails server -h` for more startup options 
Feb 26 09:17:15 myApp app/web.1:  Puma starting in single mode... 
Feb 26 09:17:15 myApp app/web.1:  * Version 3.7.1 (ruby 2.4.0-p0), codename: Snowy Sagebrush 
Feb 26 09:17:15 myApp app/web.1:  * Min threads: 5, max threads: 5 
Feb 26 09:17:15 myApp app/web.1:  * Environment: production 
Feb 26 09:17:15 myApp app/web.1:  * Listening on tcp://0.0.0.0:54743 
Feb 26 09:17:15 myApp app/web.1:  Use Ctrl-C to stop 
Feb 26 09:17:15 myApp heroku/web.1:  State changed from starting to up
```

without any Procfile. Everything works.

Ok, I solved it with file named *Procfile* in my directory. The content is:

```
web: bundle exec puma -t 5:5 -p ${PORT:-3000} -e ${RACK_ENV:-development}
```

Why with Rails 5.0.1 I don't need it?

Starting log with Procfile:

```
Feb 26 09:53:52 myApp heroku/web.1:  Starting process with command `bundle exec puma -t 5:5 -p ${PORT:-3000} -e ${RACK_ENV:-development}` 
Feb 26 09:53:54 myApp app/web.1:  Puma starting in single mode... 
Feb 26 09:53:54 myApp app/web.1:  * Version 3.7.1 (ruby 2.4.0-p0), codename: Snowy Sagebrush 
Feb 26 09:53:54 myApp app/web.1:  * Min threads: 5, max threads: 5 
Feb 26 09:53:54 myApp app/web.1:  * Environment: production 
Feb 26 09:53:56 myApp app/web.1:  * Listening on tcp://0.0.0.0:23293 
Feb 26 09:53:56 myApp app/web.1:  Use Ctrl-C to stop 
Feb 26 09:53:56 myApp heroku/web.1:  State changed from starting to up
```

Why it works now? The port is still strange (23293), it seems random to me.

And why Puma is starting in **single mode**?

> Why it works now? The port is still strange (23293), it seems random to me.

Yes, that's a consequence of Heroku's routing of requests to applications. The strange bit was the `localhost`.

So this is what I think is happening:

1. In Rails 5.0.1, in the absence of a Procfile, Heroku is running this command:

    ``` sh
    bin/rails server -p <random-port> -e production
    ```

    This gives the following boot information:

    ``` sh
    Rails 5.0.1 application starting in production on http://0.0.0.0:<random-port>
    ```

2. In Rails 5.1.0.beta1, in the absence of a Procfile, Heroku is running the same command but this is the result:

    ``` sh
    Rails 5.1.0.beta1 application starting in production on http://localhost:<random-port>
    ```

 I think this is down to a change where Rails is supplying the default binding as `localhost` as opposed to it coming from Rack where it does the following:

``` ruby
default_host = environment == 'development' ? 'localhost' : '0.0.0.0'
```

There doesn't appear to be an equivalent environment check for the Rails `server` command so it's always `localhost`.

Whilst we should probably fix this regression I would recommend that you use a [`Procfile`][1] as recommended by Heroku and also follow [their guide on configuring Puma][2].

[1]: https://devcenter.heroku.com/articles/deploying-rails-applications-with-the-puma-web-server#procfile
[2]: https://devcenter.heroku.com/articles/deploying-rails-applications-with-the-puma-web-server#config
Ok, I fixed this with Procfile file. Feel free to close. :D
We should use 0.0.0.0 when running in a non development environment with `rails -s` thanks for the report, this is a bug.

issue.title: Set correct host except development environment
issue.body:
Currently `localhost` is used for the default host in all environments.
But up to Rails 5.0, `0.0.0.0` is used except for development.
So fixed to use the same value as 5.0.

Fixes #28184

body:
As a note, you can get around this in your Procfile

```
web: bin/rails server -p $PORT -b 0.0.0.0
```

A fix has been merged into master, but no new beta or RC has been cut. The bug exists in 5.1.0.beta1 the next release should have this fixed.
